entries.description: Frames agent evaluations, benchmarks and leaderboards as held-constant ablations across three factors: Model, Harness, and Task Adaptation (none, pre-baked skill, or self-customization where the agent builds its own tools first). Use when deciding which eval cells to run next, designing a benchmark matrix, writing an eval report, or laying out a leaderboard UI so each product category gets a clear story without overwhelming viewers. Don't use for writing a single grader or task (build those first), or for generic statistics questions unrelated to agent evals.

Synchronizes all AAIF Working Group (wg-*) and foundation repositories, meeting minutes, charters, monthly reports, deliverables, reference architectures, and open pull requests from https://github.com/aaif/* into Google NotebookLM (https://notebooklm.google.com/notebook/3f4ea1ea-fe19-4afe-8cbe-ac5f9950412d). Features full state-based lifecycle management (skip unchanged, update modified, add new, remove deleted/merged) with active credential validation, bi-weekly lookback synthesis, and automated public GitHub Gist reporting.

Triages the user's unread Chat, Email, and Calendar into an actionable "pay attention vs. ignore" digest. Uses a local user profile (~/.config/agent/user-profile.md) to personalize prioritization weights, key collaborators, and projects. If the profile is missing, the agent will guide the user to create one.

Convenes three independent, cold-start subagent delegates in parallel (using configured multi-model seats in ~/.config/council/roster.json with automatic fallback, or pro-tier council-delegate subagents) with isolated context, read-only tools, and findings-first adversarial scoring, looping by default until all three delegates score >= 9/10 while fighting scope creep. Trigger on "/council", "c9" (shorthand for "keep working until 9/10 from the council"), "/council <N>", "/council once", "council", "the council", "ask the council", or common misspellings ("counsil", "coucil", "concil", "councel"). Use only when the user asks for the council or a multi-model review loop. Don't use for an ordinary single-reviewer code review or a single refute pass of a diff against its spec (use adlc-prosecutor), or for persona onboarding walkthroughs (use developer-friction-reviewer).

Orchestrates persona-based developer friction reviews on onboarding flows, recipes, tools, and CLIs. Spawns a persona subagent to follow documented steps from a cold start, records errors in a Friction Log artifact, and fixes verified issues across review loops. Use when testing developer experience (DX), walking a new developer journey, auditing README instructions, or validating recipes. Don't use for code review (use adlc-prosecutor or council), unit tests, or running agents in containers (use podman-agent-harness).

Synthesizes AI and developer ecosystem intelligence by combining Plushcap MCP (tech company engineering blogs, YouTube metrics, Hacker News activity, competitive spaces, and industry trend topics) with Good AI List (19,500+ open-source AI repositories, daily/weekly star velocity, developer activity, and category taxonomies). Use when asked to investigate AI tech trends, discover fast-growing open-source AI projects or breakout GitHub repositories, research tech company engineering momentum or blog activity, lookup items on goodailist.com or Plushcap, track developer metrics, analyze competitive spaces, or cross-reference enterprise tech announcements with open-source ecosystem adoption. Don't use for generic non-tech web search (use search_web) or single-file git operations (use vcs).

Capture Critical User Journey (CUJ) screenshots and GIFs from web apps using headless Chromium, keyed to the repo's feature map so each journey proves one named feature. Use when you need to verify UI changes through the real app, produce reviewable visual evidence for a PR, or document user flows. Don't use for component-level stories (use storybook).

Writes and tests Storybook stories for React components: one story per state, play functions, and batch screenshots. Use when asked for stories or component isolation. Don't use for building a whole UI feature (use ui-developer) or capturing app journeys (use cuj-screenshots).

End-to-end loop for building React/TypeScript UI features with agents - typed component, behavior tests, Storybook isolation, property tests for stateful UI, and feature-map-driven visual verification. Use when building or changing a UI feature or component, together with engineering-discipline. Don't use for a one-line style or copy tweak (core rules only), stories alone (use storybook), or journey capture alone (use cuj-screenshots).

Audits a whole repository and moves its rules down the trust order (structure, then verification, then prose) before agents write more code in it: lints with agent-actionable messages, directory boundaries, one blessed wrapper per nuance-heavy API, dead code and comment slop removed, a feature map, and a reusable verification driver. Use when preparing a repo for heavy agent use or an autonomous loop, when the same review finding or correction keeps coming back, or when asked to garden, de-slop, or harden a codebase. Don't use for a single feature or bug fix (use engineering-discipline), for slimming AGENTS.md alone (use checkup), or for reviewing one diff (use adlc-prosecutor).

Elixir and Phoenix coding standards: pattern matching, error tuples, OTP, Ecto, and LiveView conventions. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring Elixir code, together with engineering-discipline for anything beyond a trivial edit. Don't use for non-Elixir backends or for repo-wide boundary rules (use codebase-gardening).

Core engineering loop for any code change bigger than a trivial edit. Picks a size tier, writes a short spec whose acceptance criteria each end in "Verify:" for medium work, debugs from root cause, never weakens tests or adds suppressions, and verifies through the real surface before claiming done. Use for a multi-file feature, a bug or ticket whose cause you still have to find, a refactor, or an unclear request, and load it together with any specialized skill (UI, Elixir, security). Don't use for a new project, a multi-PR build, or a risky migration (use spec-kit-adlc), or for repo-wide cleanup (use codebase-gardening).

Secure coding rules for web apps: input validation, output encoding, sessions, authentication, authorization, and secrets. Use when a change touches untrusted input, login, tokens, cookies, or access control, together with engineering-discipline. Don't use for auditing MCP server configs (use mcp-auditor) or for general code review.

Guide and best practices for creating, evaluating, and iteratively improving high-leverage skills for AI coding agents: when a skill is warranted, trigger descriptions, structure, and eval loops. Use when authoring or refining a SKILL.md outside CloudCode. Don't use in CloudCode (use skill-author) or for packaging skills into plugins (use skills-to-plugins).

Plans and de-risks a large build by pairing GitHub spec-kit (spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md) with ADLC gates (spec-lint, premortem, rails-guard, prosecution) and, for parallel work, an agb fleet. Use when starting a new project or service, a feature that spans several PRs or weeks, or a risky migration or data, auth, or public-API change that is hard to revert. Don't use for a single-PR feature or a bug fix (use engineering-discipline), or for running one named ADLC gate on an existing spec (use adlc).

Compile, validate, and explore multi-layer structural and cross-cutting interactive graphs for stateful processes, OKF v0.2 LLM wikis, knowledge/entity graphs (KGs), and ATIF agent trajectories (with explicit blind alleys, backtrack return arcs, subagent drill-down, and cross-trajectory comparison). Use when visualizing complex systems, workflows, concept wikis, people/project/document networks, or multi-turn agent trajectories beyond ~15 nodes where flat static diagrams saturate and force-directed hairballs lose causal hierarchy. Don't use for small static architecture or flow diagrams (use diagram-design).

Create production-grade, synchronous terminal recordings (asciinema .cast) and interactive tabbed web walkthroughs for AI agents, developer tools, and CLI journeys. Includes PTY prompt-synchronization, intelligent time-compression, secret redaction, scenario banner structuring, and zoomable Mermaid flowchart companions.

Create branded architecture, IT current-state, flowchart, sequence, state machine, ER/data model, timeline, swimlane, quadrant, radar/spider, loop/flywheel, nested, tree, org chart, layer stack, Venn, pyramid/funnel, bar, line, Gantt and scatter charts, high-level, process, medallion, data flow, DP integration, or DP security matrix diagrams as standalone Material Design 3 HTML/SVG/PNG with subtle Google colors. Redraw .drawio/.drawio.png/.drawio.svg or Mermaid .mmd sources at a chosen size/detail; onboard brand tokens from a website; add semantic patterns, callouts, accessible motion, or sketchy/hand-drawn styling.

Create high-impact 1920x1080 (16:9) YouTube thumbnails and technical social hero cards from real UI screenshots using a programmatic Playwright HTML/CSS canvas. Preserves 100% lossless UI screenshot clarity while layering 3D perspective depth, percentage-locked feature spotlights, subtle dot-matrix textures, and multi-stop gradient typography.

Write, rewrite, or editorially review technical prose (blog posts, whitepapers, curriculum guides, articles, design docs, PR descriptions, system architectures, and social posts) in Alan Blount's authentic voice: the Pragmatic Builder. Combines 20+ years of software engineering experience with DevRel clarity, dry observational wit, subtle "muppet" warmth/enthusiasm, crisp analogies, and strict anti-AI discipline (no em-dashes, no clickbait headers, no callout-box spam, no chatbot patterns). Use whenever asked to write in Alan's tone, review a draft through Alan's editorial lens, humanize text to his personal standards, or write developer-facing content for his projects.

Alan's standard workflow to produce a high-impact, viral X Article for the @GoogleCloudTech brand account from a trend, architecture pattern, repo, or launch: connect the trend to Google Cloud Gemini platform + live developer context, propose title/hook angles first, draft to the proven structure in Alan's Pragmatic Builder voice (20-year dev experience, muted "muppet" warmth, dry technical wit, parenthetical asides, zero em-dashes, and strict anti-AI discipline), generate clean Engineering Graph Paper diagrams, and publish to a Google Doc on approval. Use whenever Alan wants to draft an X Article, turn a trend/spec/repo into an article, or brainstorm @GoogleCloudTech content angles.

Rewrite AI-sounding text so it reads naturally without changing what it says. Use when editing or reviewing prose for inflated claims, sales language, vague sources, repetitive structure, stock AI words, passive voice, filler, or chatbot artifacts. Based on Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing." Don't use for writing new text in Alan's voice (use alan-writing-style or alanblount_voice).

Guide for designing and implementing command-line interfaces (CLIs) that are equally usable by human developers and automated coding agents. Use when the user wants to build a CLI, apply CLI best practices, or use Go with Cobra and Viper.

Audit, author, migrate, and lint Agent Skills repositories into Agent Plugins v1.0.0 specification packages. Resolves frontmatter conformance debt, groups co-dependent skills, generates plugin.json and marketplace manifests, and enforces spec containment rules. Use when converting a flat skills repo to plugins, creating a new plugin, or linting plugin conformance.
Sub-skill for composing high-fidelity music tracks via Google DeepMind Lyria and verifying container formats.
Sub-skill for validating the artist.json metadata contract, copying files, compiling typescript/Vite templates, and verifying static client builds.
Sub-skill for drafting virtual artist backstories, mini-albums, theme-based color palettes, track metadata, and lyrics.

Primary orchestrator skill for creating concept-driven AI Pop Artists. Use when a user asks to generate a new artist profile, album narrative, audio-visual assets, local web-player dashboard, and hosted live endpoint.
Sub-skill for publishing compiled AI Pop web player assets (web/dist) to a public hosting endpoint (Firebase Hosting or GCS static website bucket) and verifying liveness.
Sub-skill for generating cohesive album cover art and track illustrations using NanoBanana.

Evaluates whether a skill, workflow, or process should be fully automated, partially automated with human-in-the-loop (HITL) checkpoints, or kept human-led. Implements Google DeepMind's Intelligent AI Delegation framework (arXiv:2602.11865) using an 11-axis diagnostic scorecard, hard gate vetoes, autonomy tiers, and an operational guardrail matrix. Use when deciding whether to automate a process, conducting automation risk assessments, determining delegation autonomy, or configuring monitoring and verification guardrails.

Diagnose and repair beads (bd) issue-tracker problems caused by its Dolt backend — including engine-mode mismatches, DATABASE MISMATCH repo-ID errors, corrupt auto-backups that revert writes, dolt sql-server lock contention, hook-timeout stash-wipes, orphaned server leaks, and schema version skew (remote-backed migration blocks or client behind DB). Use when bd won't start, daemon-error is present, bd writes revert, issues.jsonl is out of sync, untracked files vanish on commit, or bd fails with "refusing to auto-apply pending schema migrations".

Grilling session that challenges your plan, sharpens the work breakdown, and updates the beads (bd) issue tracker inline as decisions crystallise. Use when you want to stress-test a plan and translate it directly into actionable, tracked bd tasks and dependencies.

Audits, categorizes, and correlates Google Cloud & Firebase projects across billing accounts, active compute, 30-day traffic metrics, cost drivers, and Firebase services. Produces structured Markdown reports with Mermaid cost charts and actionable optimization recommendations.
Guides the identification, cleanup, and consolidation of duplicate environments, orphaned persistent disks, unlinked codelabs, and safe project decommissioning across Google Cloud portfolios.
Evaluates, recommends, and formats commands for setting hard API quotas, rate limits, Cloud Run scaling caps, and automated billing circuit breakers across Google Cloud & Vertex AI projects.
Guidelines and assistance for creating macOS applications compliant with Apple's Human Interface Guidelines regarding Input, Interaction, and System Features.
Guidelines and assistance for creating macOS applications compliant with Apple's Human Interface Guidelines regarding Layout, Window Management, and Displays.
A comprehensive macOS Human Interface Guidelines code and design reviewer. Analyzes macOS application code and design for HIG compliance.

Audits local Model Context Protocol (MCP) server configurations and custom-built MCP servers for Remote Command Execution (RCE) and supply chain vulnerabilities, specifically focusing on STDIO transport injection and malicious prompt injection. Use when auditing MCP server configs, reviewing MCP server source code, or conducting a security review of AI IDE extensions.

Author a conformant Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.2 knowledge bundle by hand or from a description — one concept per markdown file with a required non-empty type, a reserved root index.md declaring okf_version, bundle-relative markdown links as relationship edges, and the correct v0.2 provenance/trust/lifecycle frontmatter (sources, generated, verified, status, stale_after). Derives trust tiers rather than storing a credibility score, and preserves unknown keys for forward-compatibility. Works fully by hand with zero OKF binaries installed; opportunistically uses binder/okfcli/factile/openknowledge when present. Use when asked to create an OKF bundle, write OKF concepts, add trust or provenance frontmatter, or turn notes/a description into OKF.

Validate an Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.2 knowledge bundle for §11 conformance and trust-signal well-formedness, reporting everything as advisories and never rejecting a bundle for optional, unknown, or broken content. Checks that every non-reserved markdown file has parseable frontmatter with a non-empty type, that a root index.md declaring okf_version and any log.md follow their reserved structure, and that provenance/trust frontmatter is well-formed (actor convention, generated/verified shape, no stored credibility score). Prefers shelling out to an installed validator (okfcli/okf validate, factile, openknowledge) but falls back to explaining and running the checks entirely by hand with zero OKF binaries. Use when asked to validate, lint, or conformance-check an OKF bundle.

Generates, updates, and curates a CHANGELOG.md file adhering to the Keep a Changelog v1.1.0 specification and Common Changelog style guide by analyzing bd issue tracking history and git commit history.

Create, assess, and improve README.md files for public GitHub projects. Scores an existing README against a weighted rubric, gives targeted section-by-section fixes, and can check strict standard-readme spec compliance. Use when the user asks to write a README, review/grade a README, improve an existing README, or check standard-readme compliance.

Generates a structured weekly or custom timeframe commit recap for a repository. Looks for repository-specific categorization rules in .gemini/recap-rules.md or GEMINI.md before fetching git logs via git log --stat to accurately organize changes (e.g. core vs experiments). Supports optional audio generation.

Routes agentic development work to the right Agentic Development Lifecycle (ADLC) gate in Gemini (Antigravity/JetSki). Use when shaping a spec or ticket, deciding how to fan out work to models, protecting frozen rails during a build, prosecuting a change before merge, or distilling repeated review findings into defenses. Triggers on "shape this spec", "is this ticket ready", "freeze these tests", "prosecute this change", "is this safe to merge", "ADLC", "which gate", "spec-lint", "premortem", "coldstart", "rails-guard", "hollow-test", "behavior-diff".

Core operating rules for agents working inside an ADLC-orchestrated run (Antigravity Booster). Use whenever executing a ticket, reviewing a diff, or acting as part of an agb fleet. Encodes quota discipline, evidence rules, and scope discipline.
Refute-charter review discipline for prosecuting a diff against its ticket. Use when asked to act as a prosecutor, reviewer, or to find reasons a change must not merge.

How an Antigravity session decomposes a large build-out into a ticket DAG and drives the agb fleet itself (recursive orchestration). Use when asked to "build X in parallel", "run a fleet", "orchestrate this with agb", or when a task is too large for one session.
